subsystems.name: Legal corpus and retrieval layer
subsystems.role: supplies the authoritative text the model reasons over, so answers are grounded rather than recalled.
parts: firm precedent bank and clause library

subsystems.name: Reasoning engine
subsystems.role: the language model plus the tools it may call to extract, compare and draft.
parts: document parser for PDFs and scanned paper

subsystems.name: Drafting and review module
subsystems.role: produces redlines and issue lists against an agreed position.

subsystems.name: Negotiation agent
subsystems.role: trades positions with a counterparty within fixed authority limits.

subsystems.name: Guardrails and audit
subsystems.role: keeps a licensed human accountable and makes every action reviewable.

subsystems.name: Integration and identity
subsystems.role: connects the agent to the systems where contracts actually live.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and license the corpus
buildSteps.detail: Collect public statutes and reported judgments, and the firm's own executed contracts under confidentiality. Licensing and privacy rules decide what may be used at all.

buildSteps.title: Build the clause taxonomy
buildSteps.detail: Break contracts into labelled clause types so the agent can recognise, for example, a limitation-of-liability clause wherever it appears.

buildSteps.title: Encode negotiating playbooks
buildSteps.detail: Lawyers write down, per clause type, an ideal position, acceptable fallbacks and absolute red lines, as structured rules rather than prose.

buildSteps.title: Adapt the model
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune or add adapters on legal text, then pair it with retrieval so every output is built from passages that can be cited.

buildSteps.title: Verify citations mechanically
buildSteps.detail: Before any draft is released, each cited authority is looked up in a source database; unverifiable references are blocked, not softened.

buildSteps.title: Test on closed matters
buildSteps.detail: Run the agent in shadow mode on past contracts with known outcomes, comparing its redlines and issue lists with the human versions.

buildSteps.title: Bound its authority
buildSteps.detail: Set monetary and risk thresholds, list clauses it may never concede, and require human sign-off above them.

buildSteps.title: Deploy into the workflow
buildSteps.detail: Connect to the document management and e-signature systems, start with the lowest-risk high-volume work, and widen scope as measured error rates fall.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and retrain
buildSteps.detail: Track regulatory change, counterparty disputes and drift, and refresh the corpus, playbooks and model on a fixed cycle.

prerequisites.why: whole contracts of scores of pages must be read and reasoned over in one pass.
models still fabricate case citations; grounding and lookup checks are what make output usable.
playbook automation needs contracts decomposed into labelled, comparable elements.
without agreed tests there is no reliable way to certify accuracy before deployment.

prerequisites.tech: Professional-responsibility and liability rules for machine practice
prerequisites.why: rules on unauthorised practice, supervision and who is liable when an agent errs remain unsettled.

pathway.milestone: assistive drafting, review and diligence tools widely used with a lawyer signing off
pathway.unlocks: faster routine work and lower cost per contract, with human accountability intact.

pathway.milestone: agent-to-agent negotiation of standardised, low-value agreements such as confidentiality or supplier terms
pathway.unlocks: thousands of routine contracts handled with human exception handling only.

pathway.milestone: end-to-end contracting pipelines under audit and professional indemnity cover
pathway.unlocks: measured autonomy, priced risk and a record that regulators and insurers accept.

pathway.milestone: recognised autonomy for defined matter classes, with courts and registries accepting machine-prepared filings
pathway.unlocks: a genuine shift in how legal work is staffed and billed — contingent on liability and licensing reform rather than on model capability alone.
